jobs.occupation: Graduate Management Traineeship Programme (GMT) - Belgium M/W/X
jobs.description:
#Talent 

 

Launch Your Career with AB InBev: Graduate Management Trainee Program 

 

What is it? 

 

Our Graduate Management Trainee (GMT) programme is a  

• 10 months program starting in August 2027 
• 3-4-month rotations within the program 
• As a junior talent, you will work on real business projects situated in Sales, Commercial, Supply & Logistics 
• You will have a 70-20-10 learning and development approach, where 70% Learning on the Job, 20% Exposure to Other, 10% Formal Learning & Training 
Who are we looking for? 

 

You are willing to become a future leader within AB InBev, and should be comfortable with an ambiguous career track, and expect geographic mobility. The following qualities describe you: Leader. Proud Owner. Agile Learner. Collaborator. Future Maker. 

 To be eligible: 

• You must have graduated (before September 2027 and no more than two years prior) with a Bachelor's, Master's (or equivalent) degree. 
• You should also have no more than 2 years of professional experience (internships/volunteers/student jobs not included). 
• Your passion and ownership are more important than the subject you studied. 
• Fluent English is needed, as well as the native language of the country you are applying in. 
• A valid permanent visa/work permit is required in the country of application to be eligible for the programme. 
• During the 10-month program and beyond, you might be required to travel within your country of application and across Europe. 
 

We are looking for: Junior talent. Recent Graduate. Junior Manager. Professional Trainee. Graduate Trainee. 

 

How can you apply? 

 

• Before you apply, check more information https://europecareers.ab-inbev.com/programmes/graduate-management-traineeship  
• Please be advised that you will only be considered for the first application you submit, therefore please make sure you are completely happy with your choice as this decision is final. 
• There is no need to upload a cover letter - this will not affect your application. 
 

Good to know 

 

• Our Graduate Management Trainee Programme is the first step to an amazing career at AB InBev. 
• Post-Programme, you will pursue a rewarding career, often within our core functions at the heart of our business within Sales, Commercial, Supply & Logistics. 
• GMT programme will give you valuable exposure and insights into leading and transforming a successful global business. You will work on real projects with senior stakeholders to drive value and undertake a structured program to support your development as a future leader. 
 

What do we offer? 

 

Next to a competitive base salary, we put our people first by providing additional benefits: 

• Learning & Development opportunities  
• Quarterly vouchers to taste our delicious beers 
• Legal holidays + Compensation & additional days (40 Days in total for fulltime employment) 
• A unique Parental leave 
• Multiple Physical & Mental Wellbeing support Initiatives 
• Meal vouchers, allowances, gift per company policy 
• Competitive Life insurance, disability & medical plan 
• A Flexible Rewards system - (smartphone, bike lease, Extra pension Plan, etc.) 
 

Where?   

The GMT programme is available in:  ¿    Belgium ¿    France ¿    Germany ¿    Italy ¿    Netherlands ¿    United Kingdom

jobs.occupation: Fit-Out Project Manager | Workplace Design & Build M/V/X
jobs.description:
Join our team!
Space Refinery is looking for an experienced Fit-Out Project Manager to join our international team of workspace designers and builders.

We design and build people-centered workplaces for companies across Belgium. Our spaces support innovation, collaboration, and the real needs of the people who use them.

We're looking for someone who brings the same care, ambition, and attention to detail to the execution of our projects.

If you love turning great designs into beautifully executed spaces, enjoy bringing structure to complexity, and get satisfaction from delivering projects that make people happy, we'd love to meet you!
What this role is about
You'll take ownership of office fit-out projects from preliminary budgeting and construction preparation through to successful handover, ensuring they're delivered safely, on time, on budget, and to the quality our clients expect.

You'll work closely with our in-house design-and-build teams, contractors, suppliers, and clients, with the autonomy to lead your projects while benefiting from the support of a collaborative team.
What you'll be in charge of
• Own your projects: Lead office fit-out projects from preparation and procurement through site execution and handover.
• Coordinate people and priorities: Bring contractors, suppliers, and internal teammates together around clear responsibilities, deadlines, and deliverables.
• Control planning and budgets: Proactively manage schedules, costs, change requests, and financial risks to keep projects commercially healthy.
• Build client confidence by Communicating clearly, managing expectations, and creating a smooth, professional project experience.
• Stay ahead of challenges: Identify risks early, explore solutions, and take action before issues escalate.
• Deliver quality: Maintain high standards of workmanship, site safety, and attention to detail.
• Help us get better: Contribute ideas and improvements to how we plan, coordinate, and deliver our projects. What we're looking for
We're looking for a confident, hands-on project manager who combines technical understanding with strong organization, sound judgment, and a proactive mindset.

You don't need to know everything about our way of working from day one, but you should bring the experience and independence to take real ownership of project delivery.

• Proven experience managing construction, renovation, or interior fit-out projects, ideally in commercial or workplace environments.
• Strong technical understanding of construction processes, interior works, and site coordination.
• Confident in managing project budgets, planning, and contractors and suppliers.
• A proactive, solution-oriented approach: you anticipate challenges rather than simply react to them.
• Excellent communication skills, with the ability to build client trust and collaborate across teams.
• A structured and organized way of working, even when things get complex or move fast.
• Fluency in English, with working proficiency in Dutch and/or French.
• 
A valid B driving license and authorization to work in Belgium.

Most importantly, you take pride in your work, care about the people you work with, and genuinely enjoy seeing great projects come to life.

Please note: Candidates must be based in Belgium and legally authorized to work here.

Space Refinery is an equal opportunity employer committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive, regardless of background or identity.
 Why join Space Refinery?
• We're an international team of creatives and construction experts based in Brussels, on a mission to create a better world, one workspace at a time.
• We're growing our build capabilities and taking on exciting, increasingly ambitious projects. You'll have the opportunity to make a real impact, bring your ideas to the table, and help shape how we deliver exceptional workplaces.
• What you can look forward to:
• 🌍 An international, talented team of people who care about good design, great execution, and each other.
• 💪 Real ownership and autonomy, with the trust to lead your projects and the support to succeed.
• 🚀 Exciting, varied projects where you can see the tangible impact of your work.
• 🤝 Close design & build collaboration, bringing creative ideas and technical execution together under one roof.
• 🤓 Continuous learning and growth, through knowledge sharing, coaching, and opportunities to develop.
• 🙌 A flexible, collaborative work culture built on trust, accountability, and positive team spirit.

Additional assets:

• Experience with logistics or delivery applications.
• Knowledge of Google Maps, OpenStreetMap or Google OR-Tools.
• Familiarity with offline-first architecture and Flutter automated testing.
• Experience with SaaS platforms.
A university degree is not mandatory. Candidates with demonstrable practical skills and relevant professional experience are welcome.

Candidates may be assessed through a technical interview and practical exercises involving Flutter development, AI address extraction, debugging and logistics QA.

Professional references may be verified with the candidate's prior consent.
 
• Opportunity to contribute to SabilGo, an operational AI-powered logistics platform used in a real transportation environment.

• Direct collaboration with the founder and involvement in technical decisions and product improvements.
• Varied responsibilities combining mobile development, AI integration and real-world field testing.
• Opportunity to contribute to the development of a scalable multi-tenant SaaS solution.

Funded under the Cyber Funded Research programme, the project adopts a phased, rigorous approach running from January 2027 to December 2030. Over the initial two-year period, it will establish a comprehensive technology landscape of quantum sensing across all major modalities (electromagnetic, gravitational, inertial, timing, and hybrid): analysing the state of the art, monitoring global innovation trajectories, mapping technology supply chains, assessing ruggedisation prospects, and characterising the likely evolution of each sensor class towards the 2030 horizon. Building upon this foundation and a formal evaluation and benchmarking framework, the project will then transition toward down-selection: identifying the candidate quantum sensors that could realistically be tested between 2030 and 2032 and that will form the basis for later prototyping, demonstration, and field trials. All findings will be consolidated into a strategic research and development roadmap (2030-2040) guiding infrastructure investments, skills development, and partnerships, and positioning the Royal Military Academy as a national competence centre for quantum sensing.

MAIN TASKS:

• Establishment and yearly update of a structured technology survey of quantum-sensor platforms (NV centres in diamond, Rydberg atoms, atom interferometers, trapped ions, atomic clocks, superconducting circuits), including TRL and maturity assessment and a mapping of the global research and industrial ecosystem.
• Mapping of classical sensor technologies to contextualise potential quantum advantages.
• Identification and prioritisation of defence-relevant use cases through capability-gap analysis, cross-domain applicability studies, and workshops with engineering, physics, and defence-research experts.
• Definition of evaluation criteria and benchmarking frameworks combining scientific performance metrics (sensitivity, stability, bandwidth, dynamic range, coherence time), engineering integration factors (SWaP-C, environmental robustness, system complexity), and manufacturability and lifecycle considerations.
• Feasibility studies and maturation pathways: identification of technological bottlenecks, modelling and simulation of sensor performance in relevant conditions, and estimation of development timelines.
• Down-selection of candidate quantum sensors for prototyping and demonstration in the 2030-2032 window, validated through workshops with domain experts.
• Development of a strategic research and development roadmap (2030-2040) addressing infrastructure, skills and training, and partnership opportunities.
• Project management and coordination: planning, progress monitoring, annual reporting, and review meetings.
• Participation in NATO and EDA working groups on quantum sensors.
• Attending and presenting at international conferences
• Writing scientific papers and project deliverables (technology survey reports, use case catalogue, evaluation framework, down-selection report, strategic roadmap). 
SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

 

• Degree(s) required: PhD degree in a STEM field (Physics, Engineering Sciences, Applied Sciences, or a closely related discipline), preferably with a focus on quantum physics, photonics, or precision metrology.
• This is a senior researcher position: demonstrated experience in quantum technologies and in managing multidisciplinary research programmes is required (ideally 8 years of experience minimum).
 

¿MUST HAVE¿ skills:

• Strong background in quantum physics, applied metrology, and advanced sensor technologies.
• Hands-on experimental expertise with laboratory setups involving atom-based sensors, photonics, or solid-state quantum devices.
• Proven track record of leading complex R&D projects and managing multidisciplinary research programmes.
• 
Ability to deliver high-quality scientific outputs relevant to engineering applications (peer-reviewed publications, technical reports).

 

 

¿NICE TO HAVE¿ skills:      

• Experience in supervising graduate students and mentoring junior researchers.
• Experience with international research collaborations (e.g., NATO STO or EDA working groups).
• Familiarity with technology readiness level (TRL) assessment, horizon scanning, and technology roadmapping.
• Experience with modelling, simulation, and data-processing approaches for the analysis and prediction of sensor performance.
• Knowledge of defence-relevant applications such as precision navigation and timing (PNT), electromagnetic spectrum awareness, or sensing in GNSS-denied environments.
 

Personal skills:

• You conduct scientific research in an independent and upright way within a multidisciplinary environment and communicate your results in a clear, concise and precise manner.
• You take initiative, solve problems autonomously and find alternatives or solutions.
• You are flexible for change and adapt yourself.
• You commit yourself in your job by giving the best of your aptitudes in striving toward the highest quality standards and persevere when needed.
 

Other skills:

• The applicant shall have good knowledge of English (oral / written).
• Minimum knowledge of French or Dutch is an added value for collaboration with peers.
• Good communication abilities to participate and engage with various end-users.
 

Specific Requirements

• The researcher will be exposed to classified information and will therefore have to obtain the required security clearance. The candidate must consent with the background check required to obtain this clearance, which will be executed by Belgian Defence.
• Only applicants with a nationality of a country that is part of NATO will be eligible.
• Working for the Patrimony requires living in Belgium for the duration of the study.
• Travels throughout the study for workshops, conferences and NATO / EDA working group meetings both in/out of the EU are expected. 
Contract

• Expected date of recruitment: March 2027, in consultation with the applicant. 
• 
Status: Full-time employment (38 hours / week) based on an open-ended contract with the Patrimony of the Royal Military Academy (you will not be a civil servant).

If needed: 

• Please note that your contract will be open-ended, but the financing of the contract will be tied to the funding project, which is guaranteed for the 48-month duration of the project (i.e. until February 2031). The financing of your contract beyond that period is therefore not 100% guaranteed. Salary scale: wage scale NA21 (holder of a PhD degree in a STEM field: Physics, Engineering Sciences, Applied Sciences, or a closely related discipline) with valuable/relevant seniority. A salary simulation can be done here : simulateur de salaire .RMA-Patrimony applies a merit-based research career track, allowing researchers to advance in wage scale based upon annual evaluations.
• 
Holiday pay.

 

Extra legal benefits

• Possibility to benefit from a bilingualism allowance (Dutch/French) following a SELOR test;
• End-of-year bonus;
• Free DKV hospitalization insurance. Possibility of additional affiliation for one or more persons living under the same roof: spouse, child(ren) (50% of the price per additional member);
• Bike allowance / Free public transport (home-work commute);
• Meal vouchers (6€ / day);
• Digital allowance (15€/ month);
• Free access to campus sports facilities outside working hours;
• On-campus restaurant and cafeteria with democratic prices (discount on the daily menu);
• Flexible working hours within the 38-hour week;
• Teleworking possible with allowance (2 days / week max);
• Holidays: 
• 29 days holiday / year from the 1st year of contract (then from 45 years: +1 day holiday every 5 years) 
• 1 week OFF every year between Christmas and New year's Eve (independent of the annual balance of holidays).

About the role 

The Finance & HR Officer is responsible for the day-to-day administration of IVAA's human resources and finances. The role ensures the smooth coordination of monthly payroll, employee administration, invoices, payments and financial records. 

Working closely with the Secretary General and the Treasurer, as well as external service providers, the officer maintains accurate and up-to-date administrative and financial information and supports regular financial monitoring and reporting. 

The position requires a highly organised, reliable and discreet individual who can manage several administrative processes independently while working within the organisation's established procedures and approval arrangements. 

Key responsibilities 

Finances 

• Receive, organise and file incoming and outgoing invoices and supporting financial documentation. 
• Maintain accurate and up-to-date records of income and expenditure in the organisation's financial tracking system or accounting software. 
• Carry out monthly bank reconciliations and monitor the organisation's cash position. 
• Provide regular financial overviews for the Treasurer and the Secretary General.  
• Support periodic financial reporting and the preparation of documents required by the Treasurer, external accountants or auditors, where applicable. 
• Monitor expenditure against the approved budget and respond to routine financial queries. 
• Issue receipts for payments received, including membership payments and fees, and maintain a corresponding record. 
• Contribute to the selection and set-up of accounting software 
• Coordinate and process payments to employees, contractors, partners and service providers. 
• Process employee and partner reimbursement requests in accordance with the organisation's procedures. 
• Maintain a register of contracts with partners, contractors and service providers, and monitor payment schedules, invoicing and amounts against contract terms. 
HR administration 

• Prepare and submit monthly payroll information for all employees to the external payroll service provider. 
• Coordinate with the provider to ensure payroll inputs are accurate, complete and submitted on time. 
• Coordinate employee-related payroll changes, including starters, leavers, absences and changes to employment conditions. 
• Act as the first point of contact for employees on routine HR and administrative matters, including leave, certificates, employee details and benefits. 
• Maintain complete, accurate and confidential employee files and HR records. 
• Coordinate the administration of employment contracts, leave records and other employment documentation. 
• Coordinate employee admin onboarding and offboarding, ensuring that the necessary documentation, registrations and administrative arrangements are completed. 
External service providers 

• Liaise with service providers and public administrations as required. 
• Administer the relevant online platforms used for invoices, payments and financial documentation. 
• Coordinate contracting processes with service providers, in collaboration with the Secretary General. 
Other tasks 

• Coordinate general office logistics (office cleaning, maintenance, repair services...) 
• Manage office supplies, stationery and equipment. 
• Any other tasks as required 
 

 
 
Skills and qualifications 

• Bachelor's degree (haute école or university) in accounting, finance, HR management, finance, administration or a related field. 
• At least 3 years of relevant professional experience in finance administration and payroll/HR administration (minimum: finance administration and demonstrated exposure to payroll/HR administration). 
• Solid knowledge of bookkeeping, invoice processing, payment administration, reimbursements and budget monitoring. 
• Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including formulas, pivot tables, and financial reporting. 
• Experience with accounting software, including set-up, is an advantage. 
• Knowledge of Belgian payroll and employment administration (e.g. working with a social secretariat) is an advantage. 
• Strong organisational skills, attention to detail and a systematic approach to record-keeping. 
• High level of discretion and integrity when handling confidential employee, contractual and financial information. 
• Clear, professional and friendly communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with employees, management and external partners. 
• Ability to work independently while recognising when to seek guidance or approval. 
Languages: Working proficiency in English and French is required.

jobs.occupation: PhD Researcher (M/F/X) Mathematics department > SMAC Unit Project: POSEIDON-NG M/W/X
jobs.description:
PROJECT:You will work within the SMAC Unit (Simulation, Modelling, and Analysis of Complex Systems) of the department of Mathematics of the RMA and in close collaboration with the Belgian and Dutch Navies. You will conduct scientific research at university level, leading to a PhD degree, on a project entitled POSEIDON-NG.The project aims to develop a next-generation, uncertainty-aware scheduling capability (computer implementation) to assess, plan, and optimise Mine Countermeasure (MCM) missions carried out by unmanned systems. Responding to Belgium's transition to standoff, drone-centric MCM operations under the Belgian-Dutch rMCM programme, the computer implementation must coordinate multiple unmanned surface, underwater, and aerial vehicles simultaneously, quantify and manage mission uncertainty (e.g., variable detection rates, timing variance, weather windows), generate efficient task sequences and routes, and adapt plans quickly as situational data evolves. The new POSEIDON-NG engine will serve as an advanced decision-support tool for the Belgian and Dutch Navies, providing reliable, conflict-free, risk-informed mission plans, rapid replanning, and operator-oriented features such as what-if (sensitivity) analysis and clear plan-quality indicators. The resulting capabilities will improve the planning, safety, tempo, and overall effectiveness of MCM operations and support the introduction of the new autonomous MCM fleet.

This work builds on prior RMA research funded by Belgian Defence. The DAP/22-14 project (SBOS for MCM) delivered the POSEIDON prototype, a two-level mission-planning engine: a low-level module computes detailed vehicle trajectories, sensor-informed detection performance, and the corresponding execution times, while a high-level module uses this information to schedule tasks, allocate vehicles, and coordinate routes across the entire mission using combinatorial optimisation based on Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP). The prototype also established graph-based shortest-path computation between mine zones, automated generation of mine-threat areas, and a practical operator interface to configure mission parameters and visualise plans. The proposed research will extend this foundation with uncertainty quantification, a bidirectional planning loop enabling rapid replanning, scalable optimisation methods (decomposition, heuristics, hybrid solvers), and exploratory quantum(-inspired) optimisation, transforming a promising prototype into an uncertainty-aware, scalable, and deployment-ready operational tool.

MAIN TASKS:Extension of the existing MILP-based scheduling formulation with uncertainty-aware constructs (robust, stochastic, or chance-constrained formulations).Development of a bidirectional coupling between the low-level trajectory and risk models and the high-level scheduler, enabling rapid mission replanning.Improvement of the scalability of the scheduling engine through MILP decomposition, heuristics and metaheuristics, and hybrid solver designs.Exploration of quantum and quantum-inspired optimisation methods (QUBO, QAOA, annealing-inspired heuristics) for selected combinatorial subproblems.Integration of all developments into the two-level POSEIDON-NG architecture and extension of the Graphical User Interface with operator-focused features (what-if analysis, plan-quality indicators).End-user engagement: definition and validation of representative MCM scenarios together with Belgian and Dutch Navy operators.Use best practices for code development and documentation.Attending and presenting at international conferencesWriting scientific papers and a PhD thesis.
 
SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:Degree(s) required: Master's degree in a STEM field (Engineering, Applied Sciences, Physics, Computer Science, or Mathematics).This is a 5-year PhD position: recent Master's graduates are encouraged to apply; prior experience in optimisation or modelling and simulation is an asset.

¿MUST HAVE¿ skills:1.Background in mathematical optimisation. Ideally with Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) and combinatorial optimisation.2.Experience in programming with Julia, C++ or Python.3.Ability to quickly understand and navigate complex systems and established code bases.

¿NICE TO HAVE¿ skills:1.Knowledge of uncertainty quantification and stochastic or robust optimisation.2.Experience with MILP solvers, decomposition techniques (e.g., Benders decomposition, column generation) or metaheuristics (e.g., GRASP).3.Affinity with quantum computing and quantum optimisation (QUBO formulations, QAOA, quantum annealing).4.Knowledge of the maritime domain, naval mine countermeasures, or unmanned systems (USV/UUV/AUV).5.Collaboration in Software Development (GitHub)

Personal skills:You conduct scientific research in an independent and upright way within a multidisciplinary environment and communicate your results in a clear, concise and precise manner.You take initiative, solve problems autonomously and find alternatives or solutions.You are flexible for change and adapt yourself.You commit yourself in your job by giving the best of your aptitudes in striving toward the highest quality standards and persevere when needed.

Other skills:The applicant shall have good knowledge of English (oral / written).Minimum knowledge of French or Dutch is an added value for collaboration with peers.Good communication abilities to participate and engage with various end-users.

Specific Requirements

The researcher will be exposed to classified information and will therefore have to obtain the required security clearance. The candidate must consent with the background check required to obtain this clearance, which will be executed by Belgian Defence.Only applicants with a nationality of a country that is part of NATO will be eligible.Working for the Patrimony requires living in Belgium for the duration of the study.Travels throughout the study for workshops and conferences both in/out of the EU are expected.

Expected date of recruitment: February 2027, in consultation with the applicant.Status: Full-time employment (38 hours / week) based on an open-ended contract with the Patrimony of the Royal Military Academy (you will not be a civil servant).If needed:Please note that your contract will be open-ended, but the financing of the contract will be tied to the funding project, which is guaranteed for the 60-month duration of the project (i.e. until January 2032). The financing of your contract beyond that period is therefore not 100% guaranteed. Wage scale: class NA11 (Master's degree) ou NA21 (holder of an Ir degree or equivalent Master's in Engineering Sciences). A salary simulation can be done here : simulateur de salaire .RMA-Patrimony applies a merit-based research career track, allowing researchers to advance in wage scale based upon annual evaluations.Holiday pay.

WorkplaceRoyal Military Academy, Avenue de la Renaissance 30, 1000 Brussels. Occasional travels abroad for scientific conferences, meetings, etc

 
 
Extra legal benefits¿Possibility to benefit from a bilingualism allowance (Dutch/French) following a SELOR test;¿End-of-year bonus;¿Free DKV hospitalization insurance. Possibility of additional affiliation for one or more persons living under the same roof: spouse, child(ren) (50% of the price per additional member);¿Bike allowance / Free public transport (home-work commute);¿Meal vouchers (6€ / day);¿Digital allowance (15€/ month);¿Free access to campus sports facilities outside working hours;¿On-campus restaurant and cafeteria with democratic prices (discount on the daily menu);¿Flexible working hours within the 38-hour week;¿Teleworking possible with allowance (2 days / week max);¿Holidays:-29 days holiday / year from the 1st year of contract (then from 45 years: +1 day holiday every 5 years)-1 week OFF every year between Christmas and New year's Eve (independent of the annual balance of holidays).¿Advantages and interesting offers thanks to the Benefits@work card (discounts, vouchers...);¿Entitlement to services offered by the `Office Central d'Action Sociale et Culturelle de la Défense' (OCASC): among others holiday centres, discount on travel organised by the tour operator...;¿Possibility to benefit from the nursery funded by Belgian Defence (subject to availability).
